findings.reason: the done-when must name the shot's conductor geometry and the recorded response carrier as test inputs, or the node cannot satisfy the clause it is measured against.
findings.text: §6 done-when (1) says the test redraws the panels "from the conductor currents and cell moments stored in the three `panel-fields.npz` files alone", but the §5 builder it names needs two further inputs that no npz carries: the conductor geometry, read from the shot store (`benchmarks/mast_centroid_solve_panels.py:162` `_coil_outlines` opens `SHOT_STORE/<shot>.zarr`, and the npz keeps only 938 four-corner outlines with no per-circuit section mapping), and the conductor source columns the lattice is evaluated from, a 1126×101 response carrier at a GPFS path recorded only in `evidence_inputs.response_carrier` in `docs/figures/mast-centroid-capability/cpu-lane/centroid-solve.json`. Clause (2) writes currents and moments into the npz but neither geometry nor carrier, so "alone" stays unachievable and a node implementing it literally must stop or silently widen its inputs

findings.reason: the node can draw both densities regardless and the measure already requires them; only the word "recorded" is unsupported.
findings.text: §6 says "The cpu lane's state is drawn twice, at its two recorded mesh densities", but the cpu-lane receipts record one density: `cpu-lane/centroid-solve.json` names only `vacuum-and-plasma-panels-fine.png` and its `drawn_plasma_mesh` records `requested_cells` 12000 and 12353 delivered, `cpu-lane/coil-edit-latency.json` records none, and no receipt accompanies the plain `vacuum-and-plasma-panels.png`, so the second density survives only as the script default `DEFAULT_HEX_CELLS` rather than a recorded field

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the claim that the cpu state is drawn "at its two recorded mesh densities" resolves to one recorded density; every other cited path, subcommand and commit resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6 done-when (1) requires a redraw "from the conductor currents and cell moments stored in the three `panel-fields.npz` files alone", but that input set does not carry the conductor geometry or the response carrier the §5 builder needs.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — figures and receipts land under `docs/figures/mast-centroid-capability/` in the repository, and the response carrier §5 uses resolves on GPFS at the path its own receipt records.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §6 names no plan label, stage name or ticket number in a symbol, path or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause (thin contours are the 33×33 and 65×65 lattice raster, confirmed in each committed `panel-fields.npz`) matches the cited evidence, the §5 builder can produce the map the done-when measures, and the caller is named: `benchmarks/mast_centroid_solve_panels.py` `run` then `panels`, both existing subcommands (`main`, benchmarks/mast_centroid_solve_panels.py:1477).
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §6 has one deliverable, the four centroid panels drawn from the §5 map, with the producer and test changes serving that one measure.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` declares `s6` on `separatrix-spline-extraction#s5`, which is the builder §6 draws through, and no other relationship §6 relies on is missing.
